chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, who said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the Black Stone, and whether people fight over it when they are many. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is like that, then gesture towards it with your hand.'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: Gesturing or pointing with a movement of the hand or finger
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida, the eighth Imam
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ الْأَسْوَدِ: The Black Stone, a sacred stone embedded in the corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.يُقَاتَلُ: To fight or engage in combat/conflict

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fighting over the Black Stone during Hajj if the crowd is dense?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) offers a pragmatic legal ruling for the era of crowding, advising that when the risk of physical conflict (Qital) during the Tawaf becomes significant, the ritual requirement of touching the Black Stone is fulfilled by a simple hand gesture (Iram) rather than physical contact. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of prioritizing the preservation of the body and the smooth execution of the ritual over strict literalism when circumstances necessitate. The hadith underscores the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence to adapt ritual practices to social realities while maintaining spiritual intent.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Muhammad Bin Ubeydullah who said,

‘Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the Black Stone, and can one fight the people over it when there are a lot of them. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was like that, so gesture towards it with your hand from wherever you are’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muhammad ibn ’Ubayd Allah who has said the following: “I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of the Black Stone if it is permissible for people to fight, so that they can touch it.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If that becomes the case then just make a gesture toward it with your hand.’”
